full_page.content:
1946, July 11
The following is a faithful transcription of a typed note by the Servant of God, Fr. Solanus Casey, O. F. M. Cap. (added to the end of a copy of the letter of Rt. Rev. Msgr. Edward Casey to his brother Owen, dated April 30, 1940.)
"O all ye works of the Lord! Bless the Lord
NOTE. July 11th 1946.
The above was written by the present Rt. Rev. Msgr. E'd F. Casey to his youngest brother, whom he had preceeded by birth about fifteen months, Father M. J., about whom the writer is concer ned, is their second eldest brother -- now the eldest living. Owen was the youngest of ten brothers with three sister among his nine brothers ahead of him and three more immediately following. These three are still living -- now grandmas.
The writer briefly touches on dear Mother's beautiful death. May she rest with saints in Heaven. Thanks be to God for the great grace He provided her, for the ten-day fearful, yet glorious struggle, that preceeded her wonderful victory in a Happy Death
Fr. Sol. O. M. Cap
P. S. The writer of the above, Rt. Rev. Edw'd, was rescued from the Jap. Prison Los Bonos. with two bishops, 150 priest and one hundred twenty-five nuns among over 2000 prisoners. Very early the morning of February 23rd, 1943 the day on which the desperate Japps would seem to have been planing a whole-sale masacre of them; they were rescued by the MacArthur Forces. Father Maurice was nicely able and went to the First Holy Mass Celebration of our Jesuite Nephew, John Mccluskey the following June 24th and has been saying holy ever since. Thanks be to God.
"O the depth of the reches of the wisdom and of the know- ledge of God! How incomprehensible are His judgements and how unsearchable His ways ! "
Fr. Solanus, O. F. M. Cap.
